title: Slip Coding.pdf — page 33
text:
Policy Conditions
Ability to define a policy that applies ONL Y to certain locations
• Example: A policy that covers only California locations
Ability to define a policy that covers all locations but applies limited coverage (limit/deductible) to a subset of locations (Sublimit)
• Example: A $100M EQ policy with a $50M sublimit for California locations
These are generally referred to as Special Conditions
At the Policy Level
• Ability to define a condition at the policy level
• Ability to see which locations the condition applies to
• Ability to manually select the locations the condition applies to (User explicitly selects specific buildings/locations)
• Ability to use criteria to automatically identify locations the condition applies to
Examples:
• State Code = CA
• Occupancy Type = Hospital
• UserT ext1 = “High Hazard Zone”
At the Location Level
• Ability to see which conditions apply to each location (Each location shows the list of applied Special Conditions)
• Ability to manually assign which conditions apply to a location (User can override or add specific conditions)
Example 1 — Policy applies only to a subset
• “Apply this EQ policy only to California buildings. ”
Example 2 — Policy applies to all, but with a sublimit
• “Policy limit = $100M, but only up to $50M can be used for California buildings. ”
